page.text:
The Axiom of Infinity guarantees the existence of at least one inductive
set $A$. However, such a set may contain extraneous, non-standard
elements. To isolate the natural numbers, we define $\omega$ as the
intersection of all inductive sets:
$$\omega := \bigcap \{I \subseteq A : I \text{ is inductive}\}$$ By the
Axiom Schema of Separation, $\omega$ exists as a legitimate set
independent of the initial choice of $A$. It is the unique *minimal
inductive set*, representing the first transfinite limit ordinal.
